title: TAP versus the Web Bot Auth working group draft: header rules
caption: Both use RFC 9421, but TAP does not conform to draft-ietf-webbotauth-httpsig-protocol-01 (2026-10-29), or to -00 before it. TAP launched almost eleven months before the first working group draft, so the draft is not its basis.
alt: Side-by-side comparison. TAP: tags agent-browser-auth or agent-payer-auth; covers @authority and @path; no Signature-Agent required; keyid is an opaque key id; nonce and alg required; window at most 8 minutes; keys from the payment scheme's key store, whose URL the specification named as mcp.visa.com/.well-known/jwks until October 2026 and no longer names. Web Bot Auth draft -01: tag web-bot-auth; covers @authority or @target-uri plus a signed Signature-Agent header, which is required; keyid is a JWK SHA-256 thumbprint; no nonce required by the draft; expiry of 24 hours or less recommended; keys found by fetching each Signature-Agent URL directly as a JWK Set, where the well-known /.well-known/http-message-signatures-directory URL is one option; draft -00 had defaulted to that directory and also allowed a JWK Set URI or client metadata document. Each pair differs.
